title: Minority Reports: Balancing Cost and Quality in Ground Truth Data Annotation
abstract: arXiv:2504.09341v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Data annotation is an essential but costly aspect of developing machine learning-based technology, requiring multiple human workers to repeatedly label each data point in a data set. We explore the tradeoff between annotation accuracy and cost by identifying minority reports---worker responses disagreeing with the reference majority-vote label---that may indicate unnecessary redundancy, and can therefore be proactively pruned before they are executed. We develop a theoretical framework for choosing the number of repeated annotations required for a task and pruning policies at a target label quality. We estimate minority-report risk on two computer vision datasets re-annotated through a professional platform, then evaluate a rolling policy on the assignment stream to prune over 35% of repeats while preserving more than 99.9% of reference majority-vote labels.

translated_title: 少数派报告：在基准真值数据标注中平衡成本与质量
translated_abstract: 数据标注是基于机器学习技术开发中至关重要但成本高昂的环节，需要多名人工标注者对数据集中的每个数据点进行重复标注。我们通过识别“少数派报告”——即与参考多数投票标签不一致的标注者响应——来探索标注准确性与成本之间的权衡。这些少数派报告可能表明存在不必要的冗余，因此可以在任务执行前主动进行剪枝。我们开发了一个理论框架，用于在目标标签质量下选择任务所需的重复标注数量以及剪枝策略。我们在两个通过专业平台重新标注的计算机视觉数据集上估计了少数派报告的风险，然后在任务分配流上评估了一种滚动剪枝策略，在保留超过99.9%参考多数投票标签的同时，成功剪枝了超过35%的重复标注。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个通过识别与多数投票标签不一致的“少数派报告”来主动剪枝冗余重复标注的理论框架与滚动策略，可在保留99.9%以上参考标签的同时将重复标注成本降低超过35%。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a theoretical framework and rolling pruning policy that identifies "minority reports"—worker annotations disagreeing with the majority-vote label—to proactively prune redundant repeat annotations, reducing annotation costs by over 35% while preserving more than 99.9% of reference majority-vote labels.
